name: UK university careers adviser evaluating student self-service tools

context.employment_state: Employed; researching resources for hundreds of students rather than a personal job
constraints: Dependable free tools students can use independently
No assumed adviser access to student records
Needs evidence for a resource-list recommendation
context.company_awareness: Aware of careers platforms and graduate employers; evaluating tools rather than building a personal employer shortlist

trigger: Updates a student resource list after noticing that several free tools depend on university subscriptions or narrow eligibility.

searches_run.query: free job search tools university students UK careers service
searches_run.observation: Retrieval included public careers services and university resource pages. Newcastle's inspected page distinguishes free access for its own students/graduates, authentication routes and resource-specific access conditions; a stated expiry date also shows why dated checks matter.

searches_run.query: university careers service free job application tracker students spreadsheet
searches_run.observation: Results included spreadsheet vendors and university-hosted resources recommending application organization tools. These show resource-list and student self-service formats, not demand for an institutional administration product.

sources.title: Online Career Resources — Newcastle University
sources.supports: Direct inspection says tools are free for its students/graduates and gives differing login/access instructions. One access period ends 30 June 2026; continued availability cannot be inferred from the live page.

sources.title: National Careers Service
sources.supports: Retrieved public service offers career profiles and resources, illustrating an information alternative rather than a commercial tracker.

sources.title: Manage Your Applications with Free Tools — Binghamton University
sources.supports: Retrieved university resource discusses spreadsheets and application organization; non-UK example of a referral format, not institutional endorsement of Job Seek.

sources.title: Application Tracker — Cornell-domain resource
sources.supports: Retrieved resource describes a downloadable student application spreadsheet; no current quality or privacy audit conducted.

best_entry_page.primary_query: free job search tools for university students
best_entry_page.promise: Provide a plain student self-service walkthrough of Job Seek's free search, saved searches and indexed-job tracker, including limitations and links to product policies.
best_entry_page.cta: Try the student workflow before adding it to a resource list
proof_needed: Current free limits and clear optional paid matching
Account requirements and public privacy/accessibility documentation verified
Relevant graduate and entry-level employer coverage
Indexed-job tracking limitation; no external imports promised
No adviser dashboard, institution contract or student-record access claims
Stable public guide suitable for linking
New indexable resource page; account/search pages are noindex

conversion_objections: Is free access ongoing or just a trial?
Can students use it after graduation?
Does it cover their disciplines and locations?
What data must students provide and where are policies documented?
Will students understand company-first search if they have no employer shortlist?
Is it useful beside our existing resources without requiring me to manage accounts?

avoid_targeting.query: monitor all students job applications adviser
avoid_targeting.reason: Shared student records and permissions are not demonstrated or assumed.

avoid_targeting.query: student job search GDPR certified platform

avoid_targeting.reason: Sponsorship and eligibility depend on employers and individual roles.

message_to_founder: Simulation: I could recommend a useful free tool without buying an institutional platform. Give me an honest walkthrough, clear limits and current policy links so students can decide whether to use it themselves.
confidence_and_limits: Synthetic referral-user scenario, not an institutional buyer interview. Exactly two searches and one direct university-page inspection. Other queries are hypotheses. No endorsement, institutional feature, privacy certification or student-outcome evidence inferred. Resource pages can contain expired access wording. Best fit is a transparent referral resource, not adviser account administration.
